chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, who said:

I saw Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'What Allah wills, not what the people will.' So when he arrived at the grave, he stepped aside and sat down. And when the deceased was placed in his grave niche (lahd), he stood up and threw soil upon him three times with his hand.

key_terms.تَنَحَّى: To step aside or move to the side
key_terms.حَثَى: To throw or scatter soil with the hand
key_terms.لَحْد: A niche or recess in the grave where the body is placed
key_terms.مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ: What Allah wills (a phrase of divine decree)

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual practice of throwing soil during burial according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s personal participation in burial rites, specifically throwing soil with his own hand three times, which establishes the recommended practice (mustahabb) for laypeople to follow. The opening phrase 'What Allah wills, not what the people will' underscores the theological principle of divine decree (al-mashi'a) superseding human expectation, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding ritual purity and burial customs.
